runs.t: Domain-Driven Design aligns software structure with business meaning through shared language, bounded contexts, entities, value objects, aggregates, and domain models. Strategic DDD is as important as tactical patterns.

Explore domain workflows with experts, identify where a term changes meaning, and define ownership boundaries. Use aggregates to protect transactional invariants, and anti-corruption layers to integrate incompatible external models.
In hospitality, 'guest' can mean a booking contact in reservations and a person with loyalty status in CRM. Treat those as different context models rather than a single massive Guest entity.
DDD is not a mandate to create repositories and aggregates for every table. Domain modeling requires access to knowledgeable stakeholders, and poor context boundaries can multiply translation work.
